column3: NKJV renders “my mouth is opened wide over my enemies” as “I smile at my enemies.”
Close to the Hebrew; שְׁאוֹל is rendered “the grave.”
Close to the Hebrew; “his faithful ones” is rendered “His saints.”
NKJV has “against them,” where the Hebrew has “on him” (singular), and recasts the verse as separate statements.
NKJV renders “the petition which one asked of the LORD” as “the loan that was given to the LORD.”
Close to the Hebrew; הַצֹּבְאוֹת (“who served”) is rendered “who assembled.”
NKJV renders the last clause as “You make the LORD’s people transgress”; the Hebrew reads “the people of the LORD are spreading [it],” and the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; וּפִלְלוֹ (“mediate, arbitrate”) is rendered “judge.”
NKJV turns the statements “I chose him … and I gave” into questions (“Did I not choose … did I not give”).
Close to the Hebrew; “a dwelling place” is rendered “in My dwelling place,” and the meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
